assumptions: The material is the original v12 text (round 1) or the spec copy (later rounds); cross-part references outside the targets may be named under missing_inputs.
obligations.criterion: Supported when every Control rule has a matching model behaviour (or a stated reason it is not modelled) and no path is found by which permitted writes make a not-acceptable artifact accepted or published. Violated when a concrete inconsistency or such a path is shown, with locators.
evidence_requirements: model run output or attack script result
obligations.question: Control layer and reference model: are the control rules of the Control part consistent with the reference model (Appendix A), and can the main Agent, using only the writes the Control part allows (contracts, facts by the permitted writers, admission requests, publish), cause an artifact that should not be accepted to be accepted or published?

missing_inputs: Delivery §2.3 (definition of attested) and Delivery §3.1 (adapter mapping) - referenced but not supplied; I relied on Control §4.1's summary
Methods §2.1/§2.4 (sample definition, freeze document) - needed to judge whether a sample ID is bound to data content (aliasing a seen dataset as a newly added confirmation sample); not examined
Control §1.1 references DEC-01 serialization; not supplied
answers.reasoning: Close reading of Control §1-§8 against the reference model: the closed format, strictness order, effective-contract walk, execution state, producer/owning step, identity/currency, binding, checks, freeze items 1-5, achieved tier, admission items 1-6, check inputs, reuse and publish each have a matching model function, and the reference model runs clean (89/89 scenarios, 42/42 mutations killed, matching the counts in Control §8). However two attack sequences using only agent-permitted writes (contracts, admission requests, publish; B/human facts only as honest execution or an unrelated earlier approval) bind and publish an artifact that the spec itself says may bind only with human approval. (1) The 'reproduced' rule (Control §4.2) is defined over producers, which must be attested (§4.1), while the revert rule (§1.2 'content changes') looks at every attempt. The agent can deliberately make a draw unattested (declare cost 0 so reported usage exceeds it, or under-declare reads), look at its output, compute and confirm another draw, then make a cosmetic program change that reproduces the peeked digest: it is not 'reproduced', binds as newest, reaches T3C and is published without a human, contradicting the explicit guarantee at the end of §4.2 that after several artifacts have been seen only a newest not-seen-before one binds without a human. A direct revert to the peeked program is caught (pending_approval), showing the two rules are inconsistent. The draw is listed as a failed draw, so the selection is visible but not prevented. (2) The strictness order treats 'added step' and 'content change' relative to the current effective contract E only. After a human-approved contract removes a step, the agent can re-add the same step name with an earlier program (or with a pin to an old output); revives() skips steps absent from E, and the added-step row (§1.2) does not forbid a pin, so the earlier seen artifact binds again without a human and can be published under a newly added deliverable. Minor: Control §6 still lists 'adding a step with confirmation not required' although confirmation fields belong to deliverables (§1.1); and the model's freeze item 3 is stricter than the spec (a required check attempt of the artifact that read the sample but produced no result disqualifies the sample in the model, but not under the spec wording).

findings.claim: The 'reproduced' rule is defined over attested producers only, so an agent can peek at a deliberately unattested draw and later re-bind its digest through a cosmetic content change, choosing among already-seen artifacts without a human; this contradicts §4.2's stated guarantee and is inconsistent with the revert rule of §1.2, which does count the unattested attempt.
findings.element: Control §4.2 'Reproduced' (first producer of a in its owning step) and Binding; model reproduced()
findings.evidence_text: attack.py Attack A: after a2 (cost 0, usage 0.5, unattested) output X1 and a3 output X2 (confirmed T3C on S2), the revert contract is pending_approval but a cosmetic change is effective; a4 reproduces X1 with reproduced(X1)=False, X1 is checked on S1, D achieves T3C with X1 and publish succeeds (failed_draws=1 is the only trace). Fix: define 'reproduced' against the first attempt of the step whose terminal fact output the digest (any end state or attestation), consistent with revives().

findings.claim: The strictness order judges 'added step' and 'content change' only relative to the current effective contract, so a step name removed by an approved contract can be re-added by the agent with an earlier program (a revert) or with a pin to an old output, re-binding an already-seen artifact without human approval; the added-step row also does not require pin to be none.
findings.element: Control §1.2 rows 'each step N adds' and 'content changes'; model contract_at_least_as_strict (487-491) and revives (523-526, skips steps absent from E)
findings.evidence_text: attack.py Attack B: after human-approved removal of 'alt', an agent contract re-adding alt with program pAlt1 (A1's program) and deliverable D2 is 'effective'; bound(alt)=A1 over the newer A2; publish D2 with A1 succeeds. Variant with pin='A1' is also effective. Fix: apply the revert check to every earlier intent of that step name regardless of E, and require pin none for an added step (or treat re-adding a previously existing step name as needing approval).

findings.claim: Control §6 still lists 'adding a step with confirmation not required' as a non-strict change, but confirmation required is a deliverable field (§1.1, §1.2 rows on deliverables), not a step field; the list should name 'a deliverable that becomes T3C with confirmation or independent confirmation not required'.
findings.evidence_text: §1.1 line 33 states the two confirmation fields are fields of the deliverable, not of its step; §1.2 lines 62-64 and model contract_at_least_as_strict 499-503 apply them per deliverable.

findings.claim: The model's freeze item 3 is stricter than the spec: it attributes an exposure to 'required check attempts of this artifact' only when that attempt produced a result on the artifact, so a required check attempt that read the confirmation sample and failed in execution disqualifies the sample; the spec wording allows it. Also item 4 is checked against any other target rather than 'another artifact of the same step'. Conservative, but an unreported spec/model discrepancy (Control §0 asks for it to be reported).
findings.evidence_text: attack2.py: c1 (required check of X1, reads S1, receipt failure, no result), then c2 passes on S1: checks_state ok, freeze_ok False, achieved T3E.

suggested_obligations: Whether a sample ID is bound to its data content (digest), so that data already seen cannot be re-declared under a new name as a newly added confirmation sample by an automatically effective (stricter) contract, in M2/M3 as well as M1.
Whether deliverables and checked steps added by later contracts (with agent-chosen required checks) should need human confirmation under M2/M3, given that the first contract does.
Whether a deliberately unattested 'peek' draw (under-declared cost or reads) should count against the check-before-recompute rule rather than only being reported as a failed draw.
